Episode 38 of a daily journey through the universe. 🌑
We fly with Apollo 11: the July 20, 1969 landing, a guidance computer with about 4 KB of memory, alarms during the descent, under a minute of fuel left, and 650 million people watching.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 39: Next stop, Artemis II. The farthest humans have ever gone.

segments.text: Episode thirty-eight. Next stop... Apollo eleven.
On July twentieth, nineteen sixty-nine, Apollo eleven landed on the Moon.
segments.headline: July 20, 1969

segments.text: Its guidance computer had about four kilobytes of memory.

visual.label: of memory
visual.sub: Your phone has millions of times more

segments.text: During the landing, alarms went off as the computer was overloaded. Armstrong steered past a field of boulders by hand.
segments.headline: Alarms during landing

segments.text: They touched down with less than a minute of fuel left.
About six hundred fifty million people watched on TV.
segments.headline: 650 million watched

segments.text: Tomorrow, humans return to the Moon's neighborhood. Next stop: Artemis two, the farthest humans have ever gone. Follow, so you don't miss episode thirty-nine.
